copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Tuesday, overnight UTC kickoff, brings Norway and Senegal together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Senegal side, by +13.5pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

The Elo prior reads Norway 1760 vs Senegal 1790: 30 points in favour of Senegal, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Norway to win at 33%, the draw at 28%, and Senegal to win at 39%. The away side reads 39% on this distribution — the model's central case for Senegal.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Norway to win at 48%, the draw at 25%, and Senegal to win at 26%. Polymarket has Senegal at 26%, which prices out at American odds of +292; the model has the same side at 39%. The +13.5pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Senegal side that lower bound is 32% — +6.3pp clear of the market's 26%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Senegal priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 32 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives Senegal a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +13.5pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Senegal side, not a blanket read on the market.
copy.summary: A +13.5pp gap across model and market on the Senegal side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Senegal at 39%; Polymarket sits at 26%.
copy.title: Norway v Senegal · the model leans Senegal
